research_rationale: EO 10057 (May 14, 1949, 14 FR 2585) transferred to the American Battle Monuments Commission the administration of fourteen World War II military cemeteries overseas, with supplies and cemetery records, effective cemetery by cemetery when the Army finished its operational mission and in no instance later than December 31, 1951 (paragraph 1); reserved the Army's right to re-enter the cemeteries for exhumations or reinterments after the transfer (paragraph 2); and provided a transfer of unexpended Army appropriation balances for use before a stated date (paragraph 3). I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span) and the dossier inventory of three numbered paragraphs is complete. EO 10087 of December 3, 1949 (14 FR 7287, held Federal Register text) amended paragraphs 1 and 3 to read as set out; this is a strike-and-insert style rewrite, so paragraphs 1 and 3 continue as amended and EO 10087 is recorded as a later event with before and after text, not an end. Ends: paragraph 3 is a time-limited authority for the Director of the Bureau of the Budget; its own terms confine transfers to use before July 1, 1949 (original) and, after EO 10087, before July 1, 1950, so it is terminated by its own terms (recorded inclusive, 1949-06-30 for the original window; the exclusive reading is the start of July 1, 1949); EO 10087 re-set the window on December 3, 1949, after the first window had closed, and the second window closed on 1950-06-30 inclusive. No source held shows whether any balances were transferred, so no performance date is claimed. Paragraphs 1 and 2 have no end date or condition other than the paragraph 1 transfer timetable. Paragraph 1 is a performed, self-executing transfer whose per-cemetery effective dates are not held; its outer bound is 1951-12-31 and the allocation of administration to the Commission persists. Current predicate: the U.S. Code in force (36 U.S.C. 2111(b)(1)(A), held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t36-s2111.txt, and the same section's notes, which set out EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 as provided) refers to the duties and powers transferred to the Commission by EO 10057 as amended by EO 10087 and does not repeal them; the lookup shows the Code's four hits on this order, and the OFR-catalog search reports only EO 10087 and a mis-citation. The held Federal Register texts of EO 10087 and 10088 cite this order (10088 only prints on the same page). I found no revocation or supersession in the held orders. Route: original_plus_bounded_search with the amendment attached; the Code text is a continuation lead read by me, not a packet evidence record. Limit: the Code edition stops at 2026-10-09 and the held texts are Federal Register text layers. Nothing here is a certification.
savings_reason: The transfer of the cemeteries' administration, records and supplies to the American Battle Monuments Commission was carried out under paragraph 1 by the latest on December 31, 1951 and the Commission's resulting duties continue; paragraph 2's Army re-entry right continues for the transferred cemeteries; the paragraph 3 fund transfers, if any were made, are accrued consequences of an expired authority. The order has no express savings clause, and no source held shows the exact transfer or fund-transfer dates.
earlier_end_check: The only own-terms ends are paragraph 3's use windows (before July 1, 1949, re-set by EO 10087 to before July 1, 1950) and the paragraph 1 outer date of December 31, 1951 for the transfers to take effect, which is a deadline for performance and not an end of the Commission's functions. EO 10087 amends and does not revoke; no other held order names EO 10057 (searched held texts: EO 10087, EO 10088 which only shares a page, the 1989 OFR snapshot and the Code). An earlier revocation or supersession is not shown.
scope_check: Paragraph 1 (transfer of functions with supplies and records), paragraph 2 (Army re-entry right) and paragraph 3 (fund transfer) are distinct commands. The inventory excludes only the preamble authority recital (section 12 of the act of March 4, 1923) and the signature. EO 10087 touches paragraphs 1 and 3 only; paragraph 2 was never amended.
independent_command_check: Paragraph 2 depends on paragraph 1 only for the effective date of each transfer and is separately a standing Army right; it does not end with the paragraph 3 fund authority. Paragraph 1's supplies and records transfers are part of the same transfer command. The fund transfer in paragraph 3 is independent and time-limited.
savings_check: No savings clause in the order; the savings description above records the accrued and transferred consequences and their sources. Nothing in the 2026-10-28 evidence ruling lets a later general rule end the surviving allocation of functions, and none was found.

research_rationale: EO 10104 (Feb. 1, 1950, 15 FR 597) is a standing definition order: relying on 18 U.S.C. 795 and 797 it defines as vital military and naval installations or equipment requiring protection against general dissemination of information classified installations and equipment within listed areas (item 1), classified equipment (item 2) and classified documents (item 3). I read the held Federal Register text layer of the complete order (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10104.txt, verified whole-order span) and the dossier inventory (lead paragraph, item 1 with subparagraphs (a) to (f), items 2 and 3) covers each operative provision; the two WHEREAS recitals only quote the statutes and are not operative, and the closing sentence superseding EO 8381 sits inside the item 3 span. Earlier-end tests: the dossier records no own-terms end, no change provision, no conflict and no chain event. I searched the held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals) for the number 10104: the only hits that name this order are EOs 10102 and 10103, whose held page images overlap the page that prints this order, plus unrelated page, document and hash numbers; the lookup also lists the 1989 OFR codification snapshot, a DoD regulation text, and 36 CFR 902.51, none of which end the order. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09 with laws to 2026-10-14 not reflected; eCFR as of 2026-10-14; OFR catalog and saved order texts, 0 later-event hits) name no amendment, revocation or supersession. Route: original_plus_bounded_search. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 18 U.S.C. 795 without an ending statement and 36 CFR 902.51 lists it among Executive orders under which records may be kept secret; both are leads for continuation, not the basis. Limit: displacement by a later statute or an unnumbered action cannot be excluded beyond those bounded searches, and the U.S. Code edition stops at 2026-10-09. The text is a Federal Register text layer, not a page-checked image. Nothing here is a certification.
savings_reason: The only transitional event is the closing supersession of EO 8381 of March 22, 1940, which took effect with this order's signing on February 1, 1950 and is not a continuing command of this order; no savings or residual clause exists in the held text, and no later instrument touching this order was found in the bounded searches, so no accrued right or pending action is left outside the claim.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end. The order has no sunset, condition, emergency-duration or report term in its text; no held later order amends, revokes or supersedes it (number search of the held Federal Register texts and the three bounded machine searches); the supersession of EO 8381 is an act done by this order, not an end of it.
scope_check: Each of the ten scopes (lead, item 1, subparagraphs (a) to (f), item 2, item 3) is a separate definition clause that applies to its own class of installations, equipment or documents; none is limited in time or to a transaction, and the closing supersession sentence is read within item 3's span as an executed act. The recitals are not operative clauses.
independent_command_check: The items are independent definitions under 18 U.S.C. 795 and 797 and none depends on another surviving or ending, except that subparagraphs (a) to (f) qualify item 1; the exception in (c) for the airspace reservation of EO 10092 of December 17, 1949 narrows but does not end the clause.
savings_check: The order has no saving clause; its only executed act is the supersession of EO 8381, which is not a retained command and needs no savings. The 18 U.S.C. 797 thirty-day rule recited in the preamble is statutory, not an obligation created by the order.

research_rationale: EO 10153 (Aug. 17, 1950, 15 FR 5492) prescribes under section 201(e) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949 the regulations on the travel time that counts as active duty for members of the uniformed services called to active duty for more than thirty days: section 1 (public transport schedules), section 2 (private conveyance: one day per 300 miles, fractions over 150 miles, not authorized when the call is under ninety consecutive days), section 3 (Secretaries may prescribe uniform supplementary regulations) and section 4 (effective September 1, 1950). I read the held Federal Register text layer (verified whole-order span 1214 to 3732). The dossier inventory was a single sole-paragraph clause; I replaced it with four section clauses (lead and section 1 together, section 2, section 3, section 4) at absolute character offsets of the held text so each section has its own state. Later events (both held as Federal Register texts): EO 10649 of Dec. 28, 1955 (20 FR 10095), effective January 1, 1956 under its paragraph 2, rewrote sections 1 and 2 (section 1 for travel from home to first duty station, section 2 for travel from last duty station to home, without regard to actual performance); EO 12683 of July 21, 1989 (54 FR 31162) rewrote section 1 into a single rule tied to allowable travel time and Secretaries' regulations, deleted section 2 and renumbered sections 3 and 4 as sections 2 and 3. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the rewrites of section 1 are amendments (recorded as later events with before and after text) and the clause continues; the deletion of section 2 is an express ending, dated July 21, 1989 (no delayed effective date appears in EO 12683; it was published July 26, 1989). Section 4 is an effective-date clause spent when the order took effect on 1950-09-01. Searches: number search of the held Federal Register order texts and the lookup show only EO 10649, EO 12683 and the 1989 OFR snapshot naming this order; the three bounded machine searches have 0 U.S. Code hits, 0 eCFR hits and 2 OFR-catalog hits (the two amendments). Route: original_plus_bounded_search, with both amendments attached. Limits: no current text of 37 U.S.C. 204(b) (cited by EO 12683 as authority) is held and the Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere, so continuation rests on the absence of any held ending and on EO 12683 re-basing the authority in 1989; displacement by a later statute or unnumbered action cannot be excluded. The texts are Federal Register text layers, not page-checked images. Nothing here is a certification.
savings_reason: The order has no savings clause. Section 2's deletion by EO 12683 leaves the earlier-period travel time already credited as active duty untouched by any held source; no held source states a transition rule, so no pending right or accrued credit is claimed, and the surviving sections are carried as operative.
earlier_end_check: Section 2 ended by EO 12683's express deletion on 1989-07-21 (no earlier end shown; EO 10649 rewrote rather than ended it). Section 4 ended on its own date, 1950-09-01. Sections 1 and 3 have no own-terms end, and no held order revokes or supersedes EO 10153; EO 10649 and EO 12683 amend it and each says so. A search of the held orders for the number 10153 found no other citing order.
scope_check: Four sections, four scopes: lead with section 1, section 2, section 3, section 4. EO 12683's renumbering (old sections 3 and 4 become sections 2 and 3) is recorded as a later event of the surviving clauses and does not change which clause is which; the dossier's whole-order clause was replaced because it hid section 2's separate end.
independent_command_check: Section 3 (Secretaries' supplementary regulations) is independent of sections 1 and 2 and continues after section 2 was deleted; section 4's effective date is independent of the substantive sections and ended by arrival of the date. Section 1 and section 2 were separate commands: section 2 was removed in 1989 without ending section 1.
savings_check: No savings clause in any of the three instruments; the 1989 deletion and rewrite are prospective amendments and the packet holds no source that preserves or removes earlier crediting, so no savings is claimed beyond the carried clauses.
